task: Issue #3653: agent-facing force-push instructions use bare --force-with-lease, which a concurrent git fetch defeats, letting one agent destroy another's commits. Pin the lease to the observed head.sha and add a regression guard.

events.content: Read #3653 and #3413. Both describe the same failure: a second agent force-pushes a PR branch and removes the first agent's commits. #3653 names the fix directly, an atomic compare-and-swap on push.

Searched the corpus for force-push call sites. Found .github/scripts/safe_push_pr_branch.py already refuses --force-with-lease unless --expected-remote-sha is supplied, building --force-with-lease=<dest>:<sha>. The correct contract already exists in this repository.

Found three agent-facing documents handing out the unsafe bare form on a SHA refspec: .claude/commands/pr-autofix.md, docs/autonomous-pr-monitor.md, and the generated src/copilot-cli/skills/pr-autofix/SKILL.md.

Checked ADR-076 (accepted, implemented false) and confirmed .claude/skills/github/scripts/pr/pr_autofix_lease.py already exists, so #3413's coordination lease is largely built. The unfixed gap is the transport-layer guard #3653 asks for.

Proved the defect empirically in two throwaway clones rather than arguing from documentation. Agent A pushed commit Y; agent B fetched (the documented defeat condition) then force-pushed with the bare form. The push SUCCEEDED and Y was destroyed.

Ran the isolating control on the same repo state: restored Y, then retried the identical push with --force-with-lease=main:<the SHA B last observed>. Git rejected it with 'stale info' and Y survived. Only the lease form differed, so the explicit SHA is individually load-bearing.

Pinned the lease in both canonical documents to the head.sha the agent already reads from get_pr_context.py, and recorded why the preceding rev-parse check cannot substitute: it is a separate read, so it leaves a check-to-push window that only the lease closes atomically.
Regenerated the Copilot mirror with build/scripts/generate_commands.py rather than hand-editing it (14 commands processed, 14 skills written).

Added tests/test_pr_autofix_force_push_lease.py: six unit tests over the detector itself including two-sided controls for the shell line-continuation handling, plus a per-document corpus guard and a vacuity guard asserting each guarded document still contains a refspec push at all.
Verified the guard is not retrospective theatre by running the detector against git show origin/main content for all three files. Pre-fix: all three flagged. Post-fix: all three clean.

Left the bare --force-with-lease examples in git-advanced-workflows out of scope. They teach an ordinary single-branch rebase flow rather than the concurrent-agent refspec path, so this guard deliberately stays silent on them; flagged in the PR body instead of widened into this change.
